# Wipes, masks and irises

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Reveals cut from what is on screen: irises from a point, push and soft wipes, door splits, slices, mosaic rings and window masks. 25 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Motion-masked swap

`tr-motion-masked-swap` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · feature, loop, launch

Content changes on exactly the frame something else moves fastest (background rings whipping past, a card kicking into a tilt), so the change hides inside the motion and two states chain in one space with no visible cut.

- **Build:** Drive a large secondary motion with a curve whose peak falls on the swap frame s. Either run a background sweep on E.smooth over 20-24 f, from s − 11 to s + 11, so its peak speed lands on s. Or kick a card with rotateY = 12 deg × hitPulse(f − s + 2, 2, 3) and skewY 2 deg on the same envelope, in a perspective(900px) container. Decide the content with fd(frame) >= s, so every motion-blur sub-sample agrees, and give the new content its own arrival (a slam or a word reveal) from s. Give kicked cards a soft shadow (0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18)) so the tilt reads.
- **Timing:** Sweep: 20-24 f on E.smooth, centred on the swap. Kick: attack 2 f, decay tau 3 f, settled in about 8 f. Repeat no faster than every 48-54 f.
- **Use when:** Changing copy inside a continuous environment; cycling examples (photos, prompts, results) in a loop.
- **Avoid when:** The masking motion is weak (under about 20 px/f at its peak), so the swap shows; or the content is a counter (roll the digits instead).

### Product surface cover wipe

`tr-cover-wipe` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

A product surface (a UI panel, a window, a device) moves in front of the old shot and either passes straight through it with the scene changed behind it, or lands and becomes the new shot.

- **Build:** Pass-through: a panel 1.15x the frame height, showing the product's real UI, moves at a constant 64-72 px/f (prog with E.linear) from fully above the frame to fully below. The scene beneath switches on the first frame the panel covers the frame completely, decided with fd(frame); the motion-blur pass streaks the panel. Land: the product window rises about 940 px from below the frame to its rest pose over 44 f on E.glide, above the title layer, while the title fades 1 → 0 over 36 f, starting 16 f before the window moves. Occluder variant: during a fast camera push, time one foreground object to cross the lens on the push's peak frame, covering at least 60% of the frame for 2-4 f, and change the world behind it then. In every version the surface sits above the old shot in z-order, and its own content does not need to be readable until it rests.
- **Timing:** Pass-through: about 2600 px at 64-72 px/f, or 36-40 f; the scene switches on the full-cover frame. Land: 940 px over 44 f on E.glide (peak about 64 px/f at 31% of the move); the title fades over 36 f, starting 16 f before. Occluder: covers for 2-4 f at the push's peak.
- **Use when:** Promise to product: the UI pushes the headline off. Scene changes that should show the product itself rather than a graphic.
- **Avoid when:** The surface is a plain coloured slab (then it is a preset wipe), or the pass-through would need more than 80 px/f; shorten the distance with a cut instead.

### Reveal by subtraction

`tr-subtract-reveal` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, sting, loop

The clutter in front of the hero flies off toward the frame edges or shrinks away, uncovering a hero that was already sitting at its final size behind it.

- **Build:** Layer order: the hero at the bottom, static, already at its final size and position; the clutter above it. Each clutter item moves along the vector from the hero's centre through its own centre, its distance scaled by (1 + index × 0.1), on E.contact over 30 f. Set its travel to twice its distance to clear the frame, which keeps it under about 75 px/f until it is gone; keep that clearing distance ≤ 750 px by starting big cards near the edges. Window variant: the current window shrinks into the corner where the cursor sits, with transform-origin on that corner and k = lmix(1, 0.05, prog(f, 0, 40, E.contact)). Its opacity goes to 0 over the last 6 f, and the next panel's entrance starts 4 f after it vanishes. Staccato variant: remove one item every 5-7 f on hard steps (fd), re-centring the survivors instantly, until one remains, held 17 f.
- **Timing:** Scatter: 30 f on E.contact; items clear the frame by about frame 24; stagger 0-2 f; the hero stays static throughout. Window minimize: 40 f on E.contact in log scale (far corner ≤ 75 px/f), fading over the last 6 f; next entrance 4 f later. Staccato: one removal every 5-7 f, final hold 17 f.
- **Use when:** Ending a busy montage on the one stat, card or word. Walkthroughs that change app areas through the product's own window behaviour.
- **Avoid when:** The hero is not ready behind the clutter (it must never pop in), or the clutter is readable content the viewer has not finished.

### Soft wipe (feathered or gradient edge)

`tr-soft-wipe` · transitions · workhorse · energy calm · launch, update, walkthrough, loop · also `dv-feather-wipe`

The next shot is revealed behind a wide soft edge that decelerates across the frame (feathered), or a panel or picture washes on behind an edge as wide as most of it at one speed (gradient).

- **Build:** <Wipe frame start kind="feather" angle feather outgoing incoming /> (`feather` is the edge width in px; kind="gradient" for the wash, whose edge is 0.7 of `span`); edgeMask({ left: 250 }) on a line that scrolls through the frame. The wipe is finished on the frame its run ends (wipeEnd()), even when its edge lands a hair short of the frame: <Wipe> stops drawing the outgoing shot from there. A hard edge that pushes the old shot along is kind="push" (the panel push-wipe); a line of type keeps its edge about a letter wide (the soft-edge write-on, or the TypeLine preset `develop`).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wipe.Wipe`, `fx/Wipe.wipeState`, `fx/Wipe.wipeEnd`, `fx/Wipe.edgeMask`
- **Materials:** The photos first take a gradient-map cast that creeps in from the top-left (shadows deep, mids pink, highlights warm, strength 0 -> 70 % over 24 f), then a broad soft white wash crosses left to right (feather about 40 % of the panel width, accelerating); just ahead of the white the photos turn warm, and the warm front rhymes with the palette of the sentence that follows.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Feathered: 350 px edge at 1080p, 30 f on E.softOut (lands at about a third of its starting speed). Gradient: edge 70 % of the element it reveals, 3360 px/s at 1080p (112 px/f at 30 fps).
- **Use when:** A quiet reveal across the frame or a panel.
- **Avoid when:** A hard edge (that is the push-wipe, kind="push"); a line of type behind the wide gradient ramp (it reads as half-faded words, fade soup).

### A colour block wipes the line on and lingers

`dv-colour-block-wipe-on` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A block shoots across a line (its leading edge covering 400 px in 3 frames), leaving the words behind it, its trailing edge slower; on the second line it lingers on the last word, which cools from the block's colour.

- **Build:** Two Wipe edges (lead and trail) with different speeds; words revealed behind the lead. Anatomy: Lead edge fast, trail edge 3x slower; words cool 15 f. Sound: A pop.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wipe`
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Lead 8 f; trail 23-50 f.
- **Use when:** A tagline on.
- **Avoid when:** A second multi-hue run in the same film.

### A soft light band carries the old graphic out

`dv-light-band-wipe` · transitions · accent · energy medium · any

The diagram slides out on an expo-in while a soft band of light travels across the frame, accelerating, taking the old graphic with it.

- **Build:** <LightSweep frames={44} gain={0.55}> + the diagram's exit on E.launchIn. Recipe: an SVG fractal-noise filter stretched vertically (baseFrequency 0.06 x 0.0015) coloured to the accent, masked by a horizontal gradient, translated; bake it as a plate for render speed. Anatomy: Band about 0.45 of the width; ease-in. Sound: Voice. Materials: The light is textured: fine vertical streaks (6-20 px, plus or minus 15 % luminance) run through the band like a light curtain or a long-exposure aurora, its edge falling off to black over about 300 px; it drifts slowly, then accelerates across as the wipe (about 44 f).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure.LightSweep`
- **Materials:** The light is textured: fine vertical streaks (6-20 px, plus or minus 15 % luminance) run through the band like a light curtain or a long-exposure aurora, its edge falling off to black over about 300 px; it drifts slowly, then accelerates across as the wipe (about 44 f).
- **Timing:** 44 f.
- **Use when:** Clearing a diagram or chart.
- **Avoid when:** A glow that is not part of the band (a halo round type).

### A text-height slot opens behind the line onto the photo

`dv-slot-behind-line` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

On the word swap a hard-edged slot exactly the height of the text opens behind the line and shows the coming photo; the type flips from grey to white inside it and the caret becomes a selection block for one frame; later the photo fills the frame.

- **Build:** Photo clipped by an inset to the line's band, a colour step on the text, then a full-frame Photo fade. Anatomy: Slot about 9 % of the frame tall with hard edges, the photo blurred 4 px inside it; text ink -> white as the slot opens; caret block about 0.6 em at 40 % for 2 f; the full frame fades in 40 f later. Sound: The music returns on the reveal hit after a short dropout.
- **Timing:** Caret block 2 f, slot fades in 6 f, colour flip 2 f, full frame over 40 f.
- **Use when:** A line that introduces imagery: a new way to see.
- **Avoid when:** Multi-line copy.

### Band wipe

`tr-band-wipe` · transitions · accent · energy medium · feature, launch, walkthrough, loop

A band crosses a region (snapping up, lingering, then whipping off, or sweeping across a chart) and the content changes along its edge: the old state is erased under it and the new state draws in its wake.

- **Build:** Clip both states to the region and drive one band position b(f). The old state stays clipped to the side the band has not reached (clip-path: inset(0 0 0 b px)), and the new state draws in behind it (a line chart's stroke-dashoffset follows b). In the full look the band is a luminous light core falling off through a warm hue, screen-blended over the content. Sweep profile: a 368 px band crosses a chart at a constant 60-70 px/f (prog with E.linear, about 27 f for a 1400 px chart plus the band), starting 2 f after the control that caused it (a tab) lands, never easing out, until the chart edge cuts it off. Hang-time profile, for a full-frame band behind giant type: the bottom edge goes from 81% to 66% of frame height over 6 f on E.out, 66% to 53% over 20 f at constant speed, and 53% to 0 over 16 f on E.contact. In the hang-time profile the band's edges are flat mask edges, so they may pass 80 px/f; nothing textured rides on them.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill the band with the one accent (or ink on a paper stage) at full strength. Its trailing side falls off by opacity of that same colour over 30-40% of its width, with no light core, no screen blend and no second hue. The full look relies on glow, gradient, beige, orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Sweep: 368 px band at a constant 60-70 px/f (about 27 f across a 1400 px chart), starting 2 f after the cause. Hang-time: 6 f (E.out) + 20 f (constant speed) + 16 f (E.contact) = 42 f. The new state draws in within 6-10 f after the band passes.
- **Use when:** Swapping a data series, a filter result or a big-type card in place, when a control's tap should visibly cause the change.
- **Avoid when:** Applied to whole scenes again and again (it becomes a preset wipe), or when the band would cross text the viewer has not finished reading.

### Blob ring frames the statement

`tr-blob-ring` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, walkthrough · also `dv-blob-ring-frame`

A soft ring of one colour swirls in around the frame and holds the next statement in its clear middle, breathing (it tightens and loosens) while its centre wanders a little.

- **Build:** <BlobRing frame start hole soft tighten release wobble color /> over the statement.
- **Primitive:** `fx/BlobRing.BlobRing`, `fx/BlobRing.blobRingState`
- **Materials:** The brush blob under a word starts spinning, collapses edge-on into a thin vertical streak for one nearly empty frame, reappears as a thick open arc round the next word (ring thickness about 25 % of its radius), then grows about 3x a frame for 3-4 frames past the frame edge and settles as a breathing vignette (hole about 1250 x 1000 px). Ring body blurred 40-60 px with a lighter inner edge feathered 150-250 px; the words inside go from grey to ink and the accent word from a pale tint to the accent.
- **Timing:** Swirl 8 f from 1.6x the rest hole; hole 0.74 x 1.12 of the frame, soft edge 0.36 of the radius; tighten to 0.86 over 28 f on M.ringTighten; wobble 25 px over 2 s.
- **Use when:** A section change into one centred statement; two or three times a film at most.
- **Avoid when:** Busy frames; a statement that is not centred.

### Frame halves flip to a new ground in turn

`dv-split-flip-frame` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, sting

The left half of the frame flips to a new ground for 3 frames, then the right half (the left reverting), then the whole frame.

- **Build:** HardStep on two half-frame layers. Anatomy: Hard halves, one beat each. Sound: A snare, then a whoosh.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** 6 + 8 f, then full.
- **Use when:** A rhythmic flip into an end section.
- **Avoid when:** More than one per film.

### Mosaic iris from a point

`tr-mosaic-iris` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, update, vertical · also `dv-mosaic-ring-iris`

A ring of square cells in the accent's own family opens from a point the eye is on (a status dot, a period) and the next scene shows clear inside it.

- **Build:** <MosaicIris at origin={dot} frames={18} ring={195} cell={30} colors={mosaicFamily(accent)} outgoing incoming />. Cells exist only in the ring; the inside is tinted and soft for its first 8 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Pixel.MosaicIris`, `fx/Pixel.mosaicIrisState`
- **Timing:** 18 f to the far corner, front-loaded (E.snapOut).
- **Use when:** The outgoing shot ends on a small round mark.
- **Avoid when:** The point is near a frame edge (half the ring is lost).

### Panel pushes the shot off in two stages

`dv-panel-push-wipe` · transitions · accent · energy medium · any

A solid panel wipes in from one side to half the frame, holds while something starts inside it (typing begins), then completes the wipe; or a coloured panel floods one side in the last frames; or a hard-edged panel wipes across in 3 frames already carrying the next word.

- **Build:** <Wipe kind="push"> (its house stages are this device: the edge starts off-frame so the outgoing shot is already moving, arrives fast and settles to 0.483 of the frame in 54 f, creeps, then leaves on E.buildIn over 42 f and is cut at speed; the footage rides 0.62 of the edge's travel in the arrival; the edge streaks 0.3 of its step, and smear 'draw' (house) streaks the pushed footage, 'shutter' declares it as camera blur instead). `stages` for other runs ([{ to, frames, ease, push, gap }]: a gap holds and creeps before the next stage), `ride: 1` pins the incoming panel to the edge as a sliding sheet. Anatomy: arrival to just under half, creep, stage 2 at speed; the hard panel 0 -> 58 -> 74 -> 95 % coverage. Sound: Voice; a riser into stage 2. Materials: Both layers smear: at the fastest frames the entering panel and the pushed footage carry a horizontal blur of 25-35 px (blur = speed x 0.3), the footage pushed at 0.64x the edge speed and the panel's edge soft over about 30 px; the blur is gone by the park, 24 f in.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wipe.Wipe`, `fx/Wipe.wipeState`, `fx/Wipe.PUSH`
- **Materials:** Both layers smear: at the fastest frames the entering panel and the pushed footage carry a horizontal blur of 25-35 px (blur = speed x 0.3), the footage pushed at 0.64x the edge speed and the panel's edge soft over about 30 px; the blur is gone by the park, 24 f in.
- **Timing:** Arrival 54 f to 0.483 of the frame (the edge from 0.075 off-frame, its speed peaking a quarter of the way in at about 7 % of the frame a 60 fps frame), creep 0.13 % a frame, leave 42 f on E.buildIn; the hard panel 8 f + settle 13 f.
- **Use when:** Moving from footage to product UI; a beat that needs a hard graphic change.
- **Avoid when:** Gradient panels that are not baked and dithered.

### Pixelate out and in on the beat

`tx-mosaic-resolve` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, update, vertical · also `dv-pixelate-beat`

The shot breaks into growing blocks for 8 frames, cuts on the downbeat at its coarsest, and the next shot resolves from large blocks in 11 frames.

- **Build:** <Pixelate cut={downbeat} outgoing incoming /> (house out 6 -> 160 px at 1080p, x1.57 a frame; in from 190 px by x0.72 a frame). Static filters, one per block size; the run is declared stepped.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Pixel.Pixelate`, `fx/Pixel.pixelateState`
- **Timing:** Out 8 f, in 11 f; the cut on the downbeat frame.
- **Use when:** A digital or playful product, a section change on a strong beat.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films without a percussive bed.

### Scene emerges from white, hero first

`dv-emerge-from-white` · transitions · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A 3D room emerges from a white frame centre-out: the desk gains colour first, then the floor, the right wall, the ceiling, the window.

- **Build:** Develop per region (each region a mask over the plate) with starts in order. Anatomy: Per region masks developing in order of importance. Sound: A reverse-cymbal riser.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Develop`
- **Timing:** 24 f power-out.
- **Use when:** Revealing a set or a product scene.
- **Avoid when:** Without separable regions.

### Flat blocks burst out and reveal the next shot

`dv-block-burst-wipe` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, feature

Hard-edged blocks take over the frame: outlined square blocks explode radially out of an icon and cover the frame, revealing a textured field; blocks retreat to one edge in steps while the next frame decodes; after a click, stepped white rectangles grow out of the button leaving a dark window around it; flat rectangles in two colours pop at random places for 1-2 frames each, the next shot showing through.

- **Build:** <BlockStep blocks> with a seeded block list growing from the source box. Anatomy: Coverage 8.7 -> 95 % in 10 f, or +12-16 % a frame; blocks 280-560 px wide; 2-4 new blocks a step. Sound: A bubble pop; a UI click; a drum cluster.
- **Primitive:** `fx/BlockStep`
- **Timing:** 12-29 f.
- **Use when:** A click that changes everything; playful, graphic brands.
- **Avoid when:** Gradient or glowing blocks.

### Halves part like doors and the next card rises through

`dv-door-split-rise` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

The next card peeks up 32 px from the bottom edge as a preview, then the two halves of the current layout accelerate off left and right like doors, and the card rides up through the gap with their speed.

- **Build:** doorSplitState(f, { start, rise: { top } }): each half's `offset` (px away from the split) and the card's `rise` (px below its rest); draw the card above the halves. Anatomy: the card peeks 32 px over 12 f, 18 f before the doors move, then creeps; the doors run the measured door path (each step about x1.5 the last, leaving at about 250 px a frame at 1080p and 24 fps); the card rides up from the bottom edge a third into the doors' run, peaks with them (about 110 px a frame at 24 fps) and decays home. Sound: A pop, a hit, a punchy accent.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.doorSplitState`
- **Timing:** Peek 12 f, from 18 f before the doors; doors 30 f; rise 50 f from a third into the doors' run.
- **Use when:** Introducing the next product surface.
- **Avoid when:** Halves with content that splits a word.

### Iris from a word gap

`tr-iris-from-glyph` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, update, feature, vertical

The next scene opens through a circle that starts in the gap between two words of the line being read and grows by the same ratio every frame, so it is visible at once and accelerates off the corners.

- **Build:** <Iris frame start originFrom={{ text, gap, left, top, size }} mode="rate">{nextScene}</Iris>; start it on the hit frame. shape (with frames and to) spreads the ratios: a burst out of the point and an acceleration off the corners. scallop gives a cloud edge. Opened in a line that is moving, the iris carries its speed: the line around the circle accelerates out (launch()) and the line inside opens moving the same way at 1.15x that speed, decaying to its drift (carriedCut(f, cover, { vCut }, { ratio: IRIS_CARRY.ratio, decay: IRIS_CARRY.decay60, fast: { share: 0, decay: 0.4 } }) on the one coordinate both lines ride); the circle stays where it opened.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Iris.Iris`, `fx/Iris.irisRadius`, `fx/Iris.gapOrigin`, `fx/Iris.IRIS_CARRY`, `lib/handoff.carriedCut`
- **Timing:** x1.28 a frame at 60 fps (x1.64 at 30) from 22 px at 1080p; about 16-19 f to the far corner. Normal 1.2-1.35 a frame. Carried line: 1.15x the cover speed, decaying x0.806 a 60 fps frame (x0.65 at 30).
- **Use when:** A line is on screen and the next scene answers it.
- **Avoid when:** The line has a single word (open from a glyph or the period instead).

### Iris opens from a point already on screen

`dv-iris-open` · transitions · signature · energy medium · any

A circle opens from the object the eye is on (the gap between two words, a sparkle, the centre of a pixel field, the space under a header) and grows by a constant ratio a frame (x1.28 at 60 fps, x1.63 at 30) until it passes the corners, revealing the next scene already moving inside; a scalloped cloud edge makes the matte the subject; it can start already 40 % wide and cover in 4 frames; a pill can widen on an ease-in as the wind-up.

- **Build:** <Iris mode="rate" originFrom scallop>. Anatomy: r0 about 22 px (visible on frame one), constant ratio; scallop 9 lobes at 6-8 % depth with an 8-12 px feather; inner scene zooming; porthole variant under a header. Sound: A glockenspiel note or an orchestral stab on the first frame. Materials: Scalloped iris: about 10 round lobes on the rim (lobe radius about 0.18 of the radius), edge feathered 8-12 px; it grows from about 140 px to past the frame over 72 f (ease-in, then fast) while the footage inside is already moving; the shape that started it becomes a hole in the ground colour.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Iris`
- **Materials:** Scalloped iris: about 10 round lobes on the rim (lobe radius about 0.18 of the radius), edge feathered 8-12 px; it grows from about 140 px to past the frame over 72 f (ease-in, then fast) while the footage inside is already moving; the shape that started it becomes a hole in the ground colour.
- **Timing:** 8-18 f to the far corner; cloud iris 74 f in two phases (40 f expo-out, 30 f ease-in to overfill).
- **Use when:** Section changes; reveals from a word or a dot.
- **Avoid when:** Eased irises that start invisible.

### Next shot opens as a window; the old shot steps back

`dv-window-step` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A rectangle opens around the product showing the next shot at 1:1 while the old shot shrinks into a card on paper in a few held steps; or a framed photo unfolds from portrait to landscape in two stages.

- **Build:** <Window rects oldScale cadence>. Anatomy: Old shot 1 -> 0.94 -> 0.80 on 16 fps holds; window grows each step. Sound: Sub-bass and a kick.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Window`
- **Timing:** 15-48 f.
- **Use when:** Product-to-world transitions; a framed image growing.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth tweens (the steps are the look).

### Pixel-staircase wipe stepped on twos

`dv-pixel-stair-wipe` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A wipe in the next scene's colour built from 22-23 px square blocks advances diagonally with a random staircase edge, stepped on twos, with a faint fringe; or horizontal bands of the next scene slide in over the old with a dither-staircase edge.

- **Build:** Build: <StairWipe at color outgoing incoming> (fx/Grids): 22 px blocks advance diagonally (35 deg) with a seeded staircase edge (12 %), stepped at 12.5 fps, 80 % of the coverage in the middle on M.pixelStair (55 f); a fringe of blocks in the next scene's colour leads it (fringeAlpha={1} for a solid accent edge); a wipe seam. Anatomy: Coverage 0.3 -> 22 -> 62 -> 85 -> 99 % on 12.5 fps steps, 80 % in the middle 0.36 s; cells 8-23 px. Sound: A riser peak; crunchy clicks under the steps.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Grids.StairWipe`
- **Timing:** 16-55 f.
- **Use when:** Image or pixel-flavoured films; a beat with crunchy clicks.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth films.

### The next shot arrives as an LED dot matrix, then melts solid

`dv-dot-matrix-arrival` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Over the current shot the coming one appears first as round dots on a regular grid, each dot the colour of the incoming picture at that cell, in blob and band shapes that grow frame by frame (an ellipse, then full-width bands); the gaps still show the outgoing shot, so the two interleave cell by cell; then the solid image fades in under the dots and the dots go.

- **Build:** Recipe: a canvas drawing circles sampled from the incoming still where mask(x, y, f) is on, then the plain image by opacity. Anatomy: Cell 12 px, dot radius 4.5 px; mask = a soft ellipse (scale 0.3 -> 1.2) plus rows switching on by a seeded hash, stepped rather than smooth; the solid image under the dots, then the dots off. Sound: A tick cluster under the music. Materials: The dots keep the picture's own colours; the gaps show the outgoing plate, never black.
- **Primitive:** `fx/DotMatrix.DotMatrix`
- **Materials:** The dots keep the picture's own colours; the gaps show the outgoing plate, never black.
- **Timing:** About 28 f: first cluster 2 f, mask growth 14 f, solid fade 8 f, dots gone in 6 f.
- **Use when:** A cut into a screen, a product UI or a digital world; once per film.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; a pixelate cut in the same act.

### Title fills with the next image and takes over

`dv-type-window` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, sting

A title pushes in accelerating, punches +11 % in one frame, its letters fill with the next image, giant echo copies appear, and the image takes over the frame.

- **Build:** <TypeWindow> (letters as the window, stepped growth) with a SnapZoom punch. Anatomy: Push +6 % accelerating; punch 1 f; window 23 f; step-out 1 f. Sound: A drum hit at +45 dB on the step-out.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Window`
- **Timing:** 95 f in all.
- **Use when:** The title before the main section.
- **Avoid when:** Thin letters.

### Two discs converge and their overlap opens a world

`dv-vesica-portal` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

Two dark spheres slide together until only their lens-shaped overlap remains at the centre, rimmed in light, and the next world shows through that overlap.

- **Build:** Recipe: an SVG mask made of the intersection of two circles (clipPath inside clipPath), positions in closed form. Anatomy: Intersection of two circles as the mask; quad in-out. Sound: The beat (+10 ms); a glockenspiel just before.
- **Timing:** 12 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** Two ideas meeting; a hero reveal.
- **Avoid when:** Discs that do not read as objects.

### UI revealed inside a growing circle whose edge is a band of light

`dv-light-front-iris` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

After the logo, the product UI appears inside a circle growing from a corner of the panel, and the circle's edge is a band of light rather than a line: the UI brightens to white at the front, saturates to the accent behind it, then falls off to the ground like a scanner passing, and the UI under the band keeps full detail.

- **Build:** Iris for the mask plus a ring layer of the same radius in screen blend (a baked radial band PNG scaled by transform). Anatomy: Radius expo-out from about 150 px to beyond the diagonal; edge band 90-120 px: an inner white wash at +60 % luminance, the accent at 70 % alpha in the middle, an outer fade to the ground; the ring thins and fades as it leaves the frame. Sound: Cut on an 8th onset. Materials: The band is screen-blended over the UI, never replacing it.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Glow.LightFront`
- **Materials:** The band is screen-blended over the UI, never replacing it.
- **Timing:** 76 f; the cut on an 8th.
- **Use when:** The first product reveal from a corner or a sidebar.
- **Avoid when:** Dark-on-dark with no accent; repeated reveals.

### Concentric squares radiate at constant speed

`dv-radiating-squares` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

Square outline rings are born at the centre every few frames and expand at a constant speed, thick strokes and wide gaps, like a pulse leaving the centre.

- **Build:** Build: <Radiate start x y color stroke={75} speed={15}> (fx/Grids): square (or shape="circle") rings born every 10-15 f (seeded, or births on the beat), growing at one constant speed; swallow={{ at }} thickens them until only hairline gaps remain. Anatomy: Births every 4-6 f; 38 px/f; stroke about 75 px, gap about 98 px at birth. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Grids.Radiate`
- **Timing:** 70 f.
- **Use when:** A hub, an end card, a "broadcast" moment.
- **Avoid when:** Easing the expansion (constant speed is the look).
